scope: Complete exact frozen four-file B3 source review against prior bootstrap/worker/execution/provider contracts; no reviewer tests, new native analysis, original read, or full DLL/runtime equivalence claim.

findings.finding: SourceBackend concretely implements the existing ProviderOwner and Services interfaces; no new virtual provider interface is introduced. Its resource pack still requires actual lower implementations.
All provider objects are unique-owned; optional backing state is declared first and therefore outlives dependent providers during reverse destruction.
Execution mutex/cache/three readiness bytes, online handles/flag, library state, host values/targets/original slots are caller-supplied state; construction invents no original global defaults.
Every required lower object and stop_sources callable is validated before the implementation is published. JoinApi is validated by TrackingThreads construction.
One Execution instance aliases the exact server/online/library readiness bytes and one frequency cache; server completion publishes the same first flag online waits for.
The first worker calls the existing server source using live config.server_port, the shared server-ready byte and shared Execution; actual ServerBackend remains mandatory.
The second worker calls the existing online source with config path/profile aliases and owned module/object/online state. The wrapper binds wait and finish to the shared Execution and second byte.
Online StateRefs bind the same live executable/cookie/profile/avatar/user fields as the configuration owner, not detached copies.
Synchronous load paths are refreshed from post-configuration state at the actual main load route; the existing library phase source selects and appends loaded handles.

Worker library paths are refreshed after the original wait2 completes, so changes made while prerequisites complete are not copied too early. UTF16-to-wstring conversion is an explicit source compatibility snapshot, not native alias/allocator equivalence.
The existing main/worker library phase body is reused; only worker=false waits and publishes its third readiness byte. Existing loaded state is retained across phases.
The between-workers hook uses actual host-init source, the same configuration object and owned values/targets/original slots; actual hook effects remain supplied.
Cleanup routes reuse unload035ab0, onlinecleanup0366f0 and hookcleanup0102b0. Bootstrap.on_exit retains their existing order; unload intentionally does not clear loaded handles.
Six Services methods are source-routed; eleven policies still forward to the required lower Services object. This adds zero native bodies or native provider closures.
Worker routes are published only during register_exit after B2 native application binding is established. bind_state merely caches references and cannot publish routes or create jobs.
bind_state is accepted only once and is rejected after stop. Configuration and console pointers remain owned by the enclosing RuntimeOwner lifetime.

Raw worker function pointers resolve through one per-image gated backend and counted leases; no gate is held while application algorithms execute. An unbound late call terminates without reading the old backend.
A second backend cannot take over an existing backend route. routes_published distinguishes a never-published backend from the actual published owner.

stop_sources is mandatory and runs before tracking admission is closed. True must exclude new application/worker/hook/exit/terminate admission while allowing already-created workers to finish, without unloading their providers.
SourceBackend guards its own stop callback against lifecycle reentry; RAII restores the control flag on false, exception or successful stop.
Only successful thread drain plus atomically checked route ownership and zero route leases permits unpublish. False/throw leaves backend and B2 native binding live for retry.
Six exact Win32 SDK function pointer types support duplicate/wait/close and LastError preservation. native_join_api returns rebuilt import addresses without executing a target binary.
A stable list ticket is allocated before possibly starting a worker, preventing post-create tracking allocation loss. Each create owns a separate ticket even if Windows reuses original HANDLE values.

findings.anchor: // A generic lower Effects may have started a job before throwing.
findings.finding: A throwing create has unknown outcome and permanently poisons quiescence instead of erasing its ticket. A returned zero handle safely removes its reservation.

findings.anchor: // The lower create may already have freed context.
findings.finding: After successful lower creation only the returned handle is accessed; no Context field is read or written because the worker may already have freed it.

DuplicateHandle retains a separate same-process join handle without closing or changing the original detached handle. Failure/exception keeps an untracked poisoned ticket and never fabricates safe quiescence.
Tracking records the lower create result LastError and restores it after duplicate/bookkeeping; wait/close/control probes similarly preserve the caller error value.
Waits occur outside the registry mutex; only WAIT_OBJECT_0 followed by successful CloseHandle removes a ticket. Timeout/failure/unexpected result or failed close retain the ticket for retry.
A not-yet-returned create prevents success, as does poison. New create requests are rejected after stop, while existing worker cleanup methods continue forwarding to their live lower provider.
Tracking destruction with retained/unknown jobs or active drain is an explicit terminal lifetime violation. SourceBackend likewise refuses destruction while its route is still published.

findings.anchor: a future compiler-CRT DLL entry must call only the application layer.
findings.finding: Compiler CRT governs new rebuilt C++ bookkeeping once; this source package installs no PE entry and invokes no recovered outer CRT entry. A future compiler-CRT entry must not call the recovered outer CRT initializer too. Full ABI/EH/global equivalence remains unproven.

findings.anchor: // cancellable registrar. Application exit cleanup remains a separate source
findings.finding: std::atexit alone cannot implement cancellation. Actual registrar/stop_sources and application resource-cleanup strategy remain required; joining threads alone does not close late exit/terminate or hook callback lifetime.

limits: Actual config/file/console/thread/runtime/server/online/hook/registrar effects are required resources, not reconstructed by this composition.
stop_sources must truthfully exclude every future admission/registration; actual cancellation/unregistration cannot be inferred from a boolean callback.
Application exit-resource cleanup is separate from join quiescence; no provider is automatically unloaded before workers finish.
UTF16 to host wstring conversion introduces compatibility storage/allocation and does not establish original MSVC alias/allocator failure equality.
Control methods are serialized and non-reentrant; provider synchronization remains mandatory for concurrent shared application fields.
state_lifetime outlives owned resource components, but arbitrary peer-provider destructor dependencies remain a caller/factory contract; generic provider internals are not proved by this review.
No PE entry, exact native CRT/ABI/EH/global graph or complete runnable DLL is claimed. Generic CRT leaf work remains deferred.
